attempts.label: DANDI:000935
attempts.paper_title: Selective control of synaptically-connected circuit elements by all-optical synapses

inputs.what: Supplementary Data 1 to 6 of the article, the per-electrode spike counts behind the ladder plots of Figs. 2d, 3c, 4c, 4e, 5c, 6c, 6f and Supplementary Fig. 4c, read from the publisher's files 42003_2021_2981_MOESM4_ESM.xlsx to MOESM9_ESM.xlsx. The in vitro claims are tested on them (data elsewhere in the claims file).

Supplementary Data 7 of the article (42003_2021_2981_MOESM10_ESM.xlsx), the Fig. 7b bioluminescence series of the five imaged mice, and the Fig. 7d to 7f sheets, the paper's own per-mouse means and per-contact group series. Used in the data check, to see which recordings of the dandiset match the paper's and how far the onsets differ, and to set one of the alternative onsets of the onset sensitivity check. No outcome is decided by it. The notes of fig7f-mua-electrodes cite it in support of the onset used, and those of the two fig7d claims compare the paper's Fig. 7d series with this attempt's.

attempts.entry_title: Interluminescence in culture and in vivo (Prakash et al. 2022)
attempts.summary: The paper's culture findings held on its published per-electrode counts, as the dandiset holds only the mouse work: bioluminescence from CTZ activated or silenced opsin-expressing neurons across synapses, and cutting the connections or botulinum toxin stopped it. In mice, CTZ raised bioluminescence and gamma power rose more with the opsin than without, but gamma events were far fewer than reported (about 30 against 214 per contact), likely through detection steps the Methods leave open. The larger multi-unit rise in opsin mice did not reproduce, and under the described rule nearly every contact in both groups exceeded baseline. Whether gamma rose in superficial layers could not be tested, as the files do not say which probe end is superficial.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Prakash et al. (2022) on dandiset 000935, which holds the in vivo experiment of Figure 7, laminar recordings and bioluminescence imaging in six PV-Cre mice given CTZ over barrel cortex, three with a postsynaptic opsin and three without. The in vitro findings of Figures 2 to 6 are tested on the per-electrode spike counts the article publishes as Supplementary Data 1 to 6, as the dandiset does not hold the culture recordings.

outcomes.statement: In the presence of synaptic blockers, CTZ increases spiking of ChR2(C128S)-expressing neurons, and 590 nm light, which closes the step-function opsin, abolishes that spiking.
outcomes.source: Figure 6c; Results, Interluminescence-mediated activation of postsynaptic neurons requires opsins, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: 590 nm light completely abolished spiking initiated by CTZ

statistics.about: green light, as the Results print it
green light, as the Fig. 6c legend prints it

outcomes.notes: Under reading (a), SB + CTZ raises the counts over spontaneous activity (median 20 to 36, 33 electrodes up and 17 down, p = 0.0375, the paper 0.0369) and green light lowers them on all 51 electrodes (36 to 0, p = 5.1e-10). The sheet has three columns (spontaneous, SB + CTZ, green light), which allow both readings. The SB + CTZ test is the same under both; reading (b), green light against spontaneous activity, also gives lower counts (median 20 to 0, p = 0.0011), so the claim holds under both readings.
deviations: Tested on Supplementary Data 6, not on recordings.
outcomes.where: Supplementary Data 6 of the article (Communications Biology, doi:10.1038/s42003-021-02981-7; PMC8752598), source data for Fig. 6c

outcomes.statement: With the non-functional opsin ChR2(C128S)-E97R-D253A in postsynaptic neurons, CTZ does not increase spiking in the presence of synaptic blockers.
outcomes.source: Figure 6f; Results, Interluminescence-mediated activation of postsynaptic neurons requires opsins, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: In cultures expressing inactive ChR2(C128S)-E97R-D253A in postsynaptic neurons, CTZ generated bioluminescence, but no increase in spiking

statistics.about: SB alone (after) against SB + CTZ (after), non-functional opsin

outcomes.notes: The counts after SB alone in the cultures with the non-functional opsin, one side of the paper's test, are not published. The Fig. 6f column "Synaptic blockers (After)" of Supplementary Data 6 has 18 values where the legend gives n = 21, and it is identical to the first column of that name of Fig. 4e in Supplementary Data 4; on it the Mann-Whitney test gives p = 3.6e-10 (the paper 0.7870), SB alone median 3 (18 electrodes) against SB + CTZ median 0 (49 electrodes). The 21-value "Synaptic blockers (After)" column of Fig. 5c (BoNT-treated cultures with the functional opsin) gives p = 0.534, not the paper's 0.7870 either, so neither column is the paper's comparison group. With the non-functional opsin the SB + CTZ counts are 0 on 48 of 49 electrodes and 1 on the other, so on their own they show no increase. The raw data are offered only on request. The block is `other` as the claims file places the data in the article's Supplementary Data (data elsewhere), where the needed column is not published. The claim was not_reproduced on the published column before the first verification; it is blocked because a test on another panel's data says nothing about this one.
deviations: Tested on Supplementary Data 6, not on recordings.
outcomes.where: Supplementary Data 6 of the article (Communications Biology, doi:10.1038/s42003-021-02981-7; PMC8752598), source data for Fig. 6f

outcomes.statement: In co-cultures, blue light and CTZ increase spiking of the postsynaptic population without changing activity of the presynaptic cortical neurons, and only electrodes that respond to blue light respond to CTZ.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Figure 3d, 3e; Results, Interluminescence requires connections between pre- and postsynaptic neurons, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Blue light LED stimulation (which directly activates the postsynaptic Opsin) or CTZ addition (which depends on ongoing spontaneous presynaptic activity) by contrast, increased spiking in ChR2(C128S) expressing postsynaptic neurons but without a change in the activity of cortical presynaptic neurons
outcomes.notes: The co-culture MEA recordings, with the presynaptic electrodes, are not in the dandiset, and the article's Supplementary Data hold only the postsynaptic counts of the ladder plots.

outcomes.statement: Co-cultures with intact connections fire synchronously across the two populations with a short delay; cutting the connections disrupts the inter-population synchrony.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Figure 2; Methods, Un-cut vs Cut experiment
outcomes.quote: Representative example of MEA recording of a mature (DIV21) co-culture (i) showing synchronicity in spontaneous intra-population firing activity, but a strongly disrupted inter-population synchronicity
outcomes.notes: The co-culture MEA recordings are not in the dandiset or the article's supplementary data.

outcomes.statement: CTZ infusion causes a rise in bioluminescence over barrel cortex in both Opsin (+) and Opsin (-) mice.
outcomes.source: Figure 7b; Results, Interluminescence in vivo, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: In both Opsin (+) mice and Opsin (−) control mice CTZ presentation caused a rise in bioluminescent light production
outcomes.notes: All five imaged mice (2 Opsin (+), 3 Opsin (-)) have a mean over 0 to 1200 s after onset above the bootstrap upper bound of the baseline mean, with ratios of 1.07 to 1.71. interlum_4 is imaged for 808 s after onset once its 58 blank frames are removed. All five also rise under the two alternative onsets of the sensitivity check.
deviations: Only ROI reading (o2b), the whole frame, could be run; the dandiset records no ROI position, so (o2a) could not.
Frames that are entirely zero (58 in interlum_4) are treated as missing. Without this the onset of interlum_4 falls on the jump from a blank frame (frame 815).

outcomes.statement: In Opsin (+) mice broad-band gamma oscillations emerge with CTZ, and similar changes are not seen in Opsin (-) mice despite bioluminescence.
outcomes.source: Figure 7c; Results, Interluminescence in vivo, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: In Opsin (+) mice, we observed robust, broad-band gamma oscillation emergence that initiated with CTZ presentation ... In contrast, similar changes were not observed in the Opsin (−) control group, despite robust bioluminescent photon output
outcomes.notes: The Opsin (+) mean gamma power (30 to 100 Hz, 0 to 1200 s after onset) is 0.08 to 0.11 dB against -0.09 dB for Opsin (-), under both alignments of interlum_6 and both kept sets. The effect is small and rests mostly on interlum_8 (0.31 to 0.35 dB); interlum_6 is at 0.00 to 0.04, interlum_4 at -0.05 to -0.07 and interlum_ctrl_5 at 0.06 to 0.08 dB, above two of the three Opsin (+) mice. P against the mean baseline power, as the Methods define it, is biased below 0 dB (-0.43 dB on white noise, and a baseline mean of -0.43 dB in every mouse). Measured against each mouse's own baseline mean, all six mice rise, Opsin (+) by 0.39 to 0.80 dB (mean 0.54) and Opsin (-) by 0.20 to 0.51 dB (mean 0.34), so the statement's "not observed in Opsin (-)" holds only as the group comparison the criterion tests. The paper's own per-mouse means (Supplementary Data 7, Fig. 7e) also include negative values (cntrl 2, -0.230 dB). The rule holds under the alternative onsets too (Opsin (+) 0.09 to 0.13 dB, Opsin (-) -0.11 to -0.10).
deviations: Onsets from the whole-frame bioluminescence (o2b); the dandiset records no ROI.

The paper's errant-contact rule flags 4 contacts over all mice here (1 to 3 per mouse), where the paper excludes 7; both the union (28 contacts per mouse) and each animal's own set (29 to 31) are run, as the claims file asks.
The files are at 10 kHz; the 1 kHz LFP is resampled with a polyphase anti-aliasing filter, a standard choice for the paper's "down sampled".

outcomes.statement: The gamma increase is seen on about half of the contacts in Opsin (+) mice (15.7 +/- 10.1 SD contacts per mouse) against 2.7 +/- 2.5 in Opsin (-) mice.
outcomes.source: Figure 7d; Results, Interluminescence in vivo, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: were evident on ~half of all electrode contacts in the Opsin (+) group (Fig. 7d : Opsin (+) = 15.7 ± 10.1 SD electrodes/mouse; Opsin (−): M = 2.7 ± 2.5 SD
outcomes.notes: Under all 16 readings (band, bound, alignment, kept set) nearly every contact exceeds baseline in both groups, Opsin (+) 24.7 to 29.3 contacts per mouse and Opsin (-) 25.3 to 29.3; the Opsin (-) mean is never within 2.5 of 2.7, and the Opsin (+) mean is higher under 2 of 16. The baseline mean of P is about -0.43 dB in every mouse while the post means are -0.23 to 0.35 dB, and the bootstrap interval of a mean of 180 overlapping windows is narrow, so the rule counts small rises in both groups. As a variant, a moving-block bootstrap with 10 s blocks widens the interval; the counts fall (Opsin (+) 19.3 to 28.7, Opsin (-) 20.3 to 29.3 contacts per mouse) and the claim holds under none of its 8 readings. Under the alternative onsets the Opsin (-) mean is 27.3 to 29.3. The same rule on the paper's own Fig. 7d series (Supplementary Data 7, each contact's group mean over mice in 1 s steps) counts 25 of 25 contacts above baseline in Opsin (+) and 20 of 25 in Opsin (-), 19 with 10 s blocks; the paper's Opsin (-) group mean rises by up to 0.34 dB after onset. These are group means over three mice, which count more contacts than single mice would (25 of 25 in Opsin (+) against the paper's 15.7 per mouse), so they make the paper's 2.7 contacts per mouse hard to reconcile with the rule the Methods describe but do not rule it out. The claims file fixes the resampled baseline values as the 1 s steps, as a standard choice, where the Methods do not say which values are resampled; whether this should be an open reading is asked of a reader in questions/prakash-2022.yaml, and of the authors as a methods_unavailable finding. Measured values are for the union set, (o1a), 30 to 100 Hz and the two-sided bound.
deviations: Onsets from the whole-frame bioluminescence; kept sets as for fig7c-gamma-emerges-opsin-plus.

The bootstrap resamples the 180 baseline steps as independent values, as the claims file says, although consecutive 10 s windows in 1 s steps overlap; a 10 s block bootstrap is shown as a variant and gives the same outcome.

proposed.reason: Applied to the paper's own Fig. 7d series of Supplementary Data 7, the criterion's rule counts 20 of 25 Opsin (-) contacts above baseline (19 with a 10 s block bootstrap), where the paper reports 2.7 +/- 2.5 per mouse. The group-mean series cannot give per-mouse counts, but a per-mouse mean of 2.7 is hard to reconcile with 20 of 25 contacts rising in the group mean. As with a selection whose false-positive rate differs from the paper's, the rule as described cannot give the paper's numbers on the paper's data, so the procedure differs and the result here says more about the rule than about the recordings. The round-3 verifier did not agree. The criterion blocks the claim only when its readings differ, and all 16 give the same result, so as written it gives not_reproduced. The group-mean series are means over three mice, which narrows the baseline interval and counts more contacts than single mice would (the paper's Opsin (+) group mean gives 25 of 25 against 15.7 per mouse), so they make 2.7 per mouse hard to reconcile with the rule but do not rule it out. Which baseline values are resampled is fixed by the claims file as a standard choice and not listed as an open reading; if it were, blocked would be right. This is now asked of a reader in questions/prakash-2022.yaml.

outcomes.statement: The gamma increase in Opsin (+) mice is localised to the more superficial and granular layers of the cortical depth.
outcomes.source: Figure 7d; Results, Interluminescence in vivo, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: These Interluminescence gamma increases were localized to more superficial and granular layers across the neocortical depth
outcomes.notes: The depth order of the contacts cannot be established. The files' Position column runs z from 775 (channel 0) to 0 (channel 31) in 25 um steps, with an autogenerated description that does not say whether z is depth or height above the deepest contact. Nothing else in the files settles it, as printed in the notebook; every column of the electrode table has an autogenerated description, the electrode group says "electrode group for shank1" in barrel cortex, and the probe device says "A1x32-Poly2-5mm-50s-177". The paper's Fig. 7d source data number its 25 contacts 1 to 25 with no depth or channel, so they cannot settle it either. Read with z = 775 as the most superficial contact, the upper part has the higher Opsin (+) gamma power under all 16 readings (for example 0.34 against -0.12 dB, halves, 30 to 100 Hz); read the other way, under none. With the union set and (o1a), Opsin (+) gamma power is 0.26 to 0.95 dB on the eight contacts from z = 600 to 775 and below 0 dB on all others. The MUA rate profile, a possible independent check, is flat at the noise level and cannot decide it. Set against the paper's per-contact Fig. 7d profiles (Supplementary Data 7, contacts 1 to 25), the rise over each contact's baseline mean here is largest at shank1-electrode1 (z = 775) and falls along the labels in both groups (Spearman rho -0.59 to -0.84), and the paper's falls from contact 1 to 25 in both panels (rho -0.56 Opsin (+), -0.92 Opsin (-)). The paper's contact 1 is therefore most likely the files' electrode1 end, but neither source says whether that end is superficial; the published figure's depth axis would be needed.

outcomes.statement: Across electrodes, gamma power relative to baseline is higher in Opsin (+) than in Opsin (-) mice (mean 0.53 +/- 0.86 SD against -0.10 +/- 0.24 dB; medians 0.34 and -0.17).
outcomes.source: Figure 7e; Results, Interluminescence in vivo, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Analysis of each metric at the mouse or electrode level showed significantly higher values for the Opsin (+) group (Fig. 7e Mean gamma (dB) power across electrodes: Opsin (+) Mean = 0.53 ± 0.86 SD, Median = 0.34; Opsin (−) Mean = −0.10 ± 0.24 SD, Median = −0.17; KS test p < 0.0001; 1-tailed Mann–Whitney U test U = 4163, n 1 = n 2 = 75, p < 0.0001

statistics.about: pooled contacts, time bins and animals, Opsin (+) against Opsin (-)
time-averaged contacts, Opsin (+) greater than Opsin (-)
statistics.n: 75 and 75 contacts (25 contacts in each of 3 mice per group)

outcomes.notes: Both tests hold under all four readings, KS p printed as 0 and one-tailed Mann-Whitney p = 0.0009 to 0.0043 (U = 4504 to 5027 with 84 to 92 contacts per group), with the Opsin (+) median and mean above the Opsin (-) ones; under the alternative onsets p is at most 0.0011. Both means are within the stated SDs (Opsin (+) 0.08 to 0.11 dB, Opsin (-) -0.09 dB). The Opsin (+) median is -0.04 to 0.01 dB against 0.34, and the Opsin (-) median is within 10% of -0.17 only with each animal's own kept set (-0.165; -0.151 with the union). In the 80 to 100 Hz band the Mann-Whitney test is not significant (p 0.23 to 0.48). Measured values are for the union set and (o1a).
deviations: 28 to 31 contacts kept per mouse where the paper keeps 25 (see fig7c-gamma-emerges-opsin-plus).
Onsets from the whole-frame bioluminescence.

outcomes.statement: Across electrodes, gamma events after CTZ are more numerous in Opsin (+) than in Opsin (-) mice (mean 213.60 +/- 139.53 SD against 139.28 +/- 72.97; medians 222 and 149).
outcomes.source: Figure 7e; Results, Interluminescence in vivo, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Mean gamma event number across electrodes: Opsin (+) Mean = 213.60 ± 139.53 SD, Median = 222; Opsin (−) Mean = 139.28 ± 72.97 SD, Median = 149; KS test p < 0.0001; 1-tailed Mann–Whitney U test U = 3609.50, n 1 = n 2 = 75, p < 0.0001
outcomes.notes: Both tests hold under all 32 readings (Mann-Whitney p at most 1.1e-06; KS p at most 1.0e-07 under either KS reading), with Opsin (+) higher. The counts are far below the paper's, Opsin (+) means 28.7 to 33.6 events per contact against 213.6 and Opsin (-) 10.3 to 12.5 against 139.3, and no value is within tolerance under any reading. Measured values are for the union set, (o1a), 10 kHz, the leave-one-sample-out jackknife and the window after onset.
deviations: The event detection follows the Methods under the claims file's readings (o3) and (o4); none gives counts near the paper's, so the paper's procedure likely differs in a way the Methods do not state (raised as a methods_unavailable finding).

outcomes.statement: At the mouse level, gamma power relative to baseline is higher in Opsin (+) than in Opsin (-) mice (mean 1.16 +/- 1.09 SD against 0.03 +/- 0.18 dB), with every Opsin (+) mouse above every Opsin (-) mouse (U = 9).
outcomes.source: Figure 7e; Results, Interluminescence in vivo, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Mean gamma power across mice Opsin (+) Mean = 1.16 ± 1.09 SD, Median = 0.88; Opsin (−) Mean = 0.03 ± 0.18 SD, Median = 0.09; 1-tailed Mann–Whitney U test U = 9, n 1 = n 2 = 3, p < 0.05
outcomes.notes: Every Opsin (+) mouse is above every Opsin (-) mouse under all 8 readings (U = 9, exact one-tailed p = 0.05). The means are within the stated SDs (Opsin (+) 0.63 to 0.70 dB, Opsin (-) 0.11 to 0.13 dB); the medians are not within 10% (0.70 to 0.78 against 0.88, 0.04 to 0.06 against 0.09). Measured values are for the union set, (o1a) and MATLAB's prctile.

outcomes.statement: At the mouse level, gamma events are more numerous in Opsin (+) than in Opsin (-) mice (mean 327.25 +/- 45.58 SD against 199.33 +/- 36.08), with complete separation (U = 9).
outcomes.source: Figure 7e; Results, Interluminescence in vivo, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Mean gamma event number across mice Opsin (+) Mean = 327.25 ± 45.58 SD, Median = 304.25; Opsin (−) Mean = 199.33 ± 36.08 SD, Median = 203.75; 1-tailed Mann–Whitney U test U = 9, p < 0.05
outcomes.notes: U is 9 under 36 of 64 readings and 8 or 8.5 under the others, so the readings give partially reproduced (U = 9) or not reproduced, and the claims file's criterion blocks the claim when they differ. U = 9 holds in 29 of 32 readings with the union of errant contacts and in 7 of 32 with each animal's own set; by percentile rule, in 15 of 32 with numpy's linear rule and 21 of 32 with MATLAB's prctile. No reading puts the values near the paper's, Opsin (+) mouse means of 39.2 to 52.4 events against 327.25 and Opsin (-) 14.0 to 18.4 against 199.33. Under the alternative onsets the readings still disagree (U = 9 in 39 and 36 of 64). The open details are raised as methods_unavailable findings. Measured values are for the union set, (o1a), 10 kHz, leave-one-sample-out, after onset and MATLAB's prctile.

outcomes.statement: Across electrodes, MUA rises more from baseline in Opsin (+) than in Opsin (-) mice (mean 37.14 +/- 45.50 SD against 13.71 +/- 21.44 percent; medians 15.49 and 8.96).
outcomes.source: Figure 7f; Results, Interluminescence in vivo, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: Opsin (+) Mean = 37.14 ± 45.50 SD, Median = 15.49; Opsin (−) Mean = 13.71 ± 21.44 SD, Median = 8.96; KS test p < 0.0001; 2-tailed Mann–Whitney U test U = 3899, n 1 = n 2 = 75, p < 0.0001

statistics.about: pooled contacts, time bins and animals

outcomes.notes: The two-tailed Mann-Whitney test finds no group difference under any of the 16 readings (p 0.67 to 0.97), although the KS test on the pooled 1 s bins does (p printed as 0). Opsin (+) mean change 39.4 to 56.7% and Opsin (-) 42.3 to 53.7%; the Opsin (-) medians (20.2 to 22.7%) are above the Opsin (+) ones (13.2 to 19.5%). interlum_ctrl_4 has the largest mean change of the six mice (111.2%). At baseline the -3 SD crossing rate is 11.1 to 13.7 per s on every contact, no higher than band-limited Gaussian noise would give (about 20 per s), so the MUA counts may be dominated by noise. The outcome rests on the onset of interlum_ctrl_4. With its second largest bioluminescence rise as onset (228 s, against 206 s), part of its MUA rise falls in the baseline (19.3 against 12.1 samples per s below threshold), its mean change falls from 111.2% to 18.0%, and the Mann-Whitney p falls to 0.012 to 0.15. The paper's own series that best matches this mouse (Supplementary Data 7, cntrl 2, r = 0.990) puts its onset at 210 s, which gives p = 0.69 to 0.92, so the onset used is the one the paper's data support. Measured values are for the union set, (o1a), SD from the whole recording and every sample below threshold.
deviations: The whole-recording median of the MUA band is taken from a histogram with 0.01% resolution (a standard choice that cannot change an outcome).

outcomes.statement: At the mouse level the MUA difference is not significant (mean 77.72 +/- 47.40 SD against 27.15 +/- 18.38 percent; U = 9, p > 0.05, two-tailed), though Opsin (+) mice show MUA increases higher than, or equal to, the highest Opsin (-) values.
outcomes.source: Figure 7f; Results, Interluminescence in vivo, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: MUA differences were significant when analyzed at the electrode, but not the mouse, level ... Mean MUA (percent change from baseline) across mice: Opsin (+) Mean = 77.72 ± 47.40 SD, Median = 52.15; Opsin (−) Mean = 27.15 ± 18.38 SD, Median = 27.24; 2-tailed Mann–Whitney U test U = 9, p > 0.05
outcomes.notes: The two-tailed p is at least 0.2 under all 32 readings, so the absence part holds, but U is 6 to 8 and never 9; U = 6 (16 readings) gives not reproduced and U = 7 or 8 (16 readings) partially reproduced under the criterion, which blocks the claim when the readings differ. interlum_4 (51 to 67%) is below the highest Opsin (-) mouse, interlum_ctrl_4 (105 to 128%), so the statement that Opsin (+) mice are at or above the highest Opsin (-) value does not hold. No reading puts the four values within tolerance; the Opsin (-) mouse means are 61.5 to 77.1% against 27.15. Under the second-rise onsets U is 9 in 28 of 32 readings, as interlum_ctrl_4's change falls (see fig7f-mua-electrodes); under the onsets matched to Supplementary Data 7 U is 6 to 8. Measured values are for the union set, (o1a), whole-recording SD, every sample below threshold and MATLAB's prctile.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds only the in vivo experiment of Fig. 7. The culture MEA recordings behind Figs. 2 to 6 and Supplementary Figs. 2 to 4, and the IVIS and confocal images of Supplementary Figs. 5 and 6, are not in it; the article publishes only the per-electrode counts of the ladder plots, and the paper offers raw data on request.

The electrode table's Position column (x 0 or 50, z 0 to 775 um) has an autogenerated description and does not say whether z is depth below the surface or height above the deepest contact, so the laminar depth of each channel cannot be established.
The position of the 50-pixel ROI the paper averages next to the electrode shank is not recorded, so the paper's bioluminescence series and onsets cannot be recomputed; the whole-frame mean was used.

The ElectricalSeries description says the data were acquired at 20 kHz and downsampled to 10 kHz; the Methods say the data were acquired at 30 kHz. The images of interlum_4 are 1024 x 1024 pixels and those of interlum_ctrl_2 684 x 697, where the Methods give 512 x 512.

The image series of interlum_4 has 1111 frames, 58 of them entirely zero (between 810 and 891 s), and ends 866 s after the bioluminescence onset, where the paper's Fig. 7b series cover 1200 s after onset for all five imaged mice.

In interlum_ctrl_4 the bioluminescence onset (206 s) comes 8 s before the recorded start of CTZ infusion (214 s); in the other four imaged mice the onset follows the infusion start by 16 to 103 s. The infusion interval or the image timing of this file may be offset.

The whole-frame bioluminescence series of the three Opsin (-) mice match the paper's Supplementary Data 7 series cntrl 1 to 3 (r = 0.975 to 0.990, as interlum_ctrl_2, ctrl_4 and ctrl_5). Those of the two imaged Opsin (+) mice match exp 3 at most at r = 0.906, and no file matches exp 1 (r at most 0.68), so the dandiset's imaged Opsin (+) recordings may not be the ones shown in Fig. 7b. On mean gamma power over contacts, interlum_8 (0.349 dB) matches the paper's exp 2 (0.351 dB, Supplementary Data 7, Fig. 7e), a mouse absent from the paper's imaged series, while interlum_8 has images; interlum_ctrl_4 (-0.234) matches cntrl 2 (-0.230), as its bioluminescence does. Which dandiset mouse is which animal of the paper is not documented.

The recordings are small for unfiltered cortical signals stored in volts, a median contact RMS of 1.9 to 6.7 uV per file, and the MUA band crosses -3 SD at baseline at 11 to 14 per s on every contact, no more than band-limited Gaussian noise. This is consistent with a missing scale factor or with recordings dominated by noise in the spike band; relative measures are unaffected by scale.

verifications.reviewed: Round 3. Only the proposed change of outcome of fig7d-contacts-exceeding-baseline and the analysis behind it in the executed notebook (cells 20, 29, 30 and 31), with the claims file and the paper. The verifier did not agree with the change. Report in transcripts/prakash-2022/verifier-3-report.md.

disagreements.reason: The numbers come from the data, and the new cell applies the criterion's own rule, unchanged, to the paper's series; cell 20 adds independent support that the data are the paper's, so the gap to 2.7 contacts per mouse more likely lies in the counting rule than in the recordings. But the claims file says the outcome "is the one all readings give; when they differ the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified". Every reading agrees, 0 of 16 hold, so as written the criterion gives not_reproduced. The evidence is also weaker than the proposal's reason says. The sheets are means over three mice; averaging narrows the baseline bootstrap interval, so a group-mean series counts more contacts than single mice would, as the paper's own Opsin (+) panel shows (25 of 25 against 15.7 per mouse). The evidence makes 2.7 per mouse hard to reconcile with the described rule but does not rule it out. The Methods do not say which baseline values are resampled, and the claims file fixes the 1 s steps as a standard choice without listing it as an open reading; if it were listed, blocked as methods_underspecified would be right. Keep the methods_unavailable finding and the cell 30 numbers in the notes.

paper_notes.statement: The notes of the Fig. 7d sheets of Supplementary Data 7 give the band as 30 to 100 Hz, where the Fig. 7d legend gives 80 to 100 Hz.

The Methods' rule for errant contacts (RMS beyond 3 IQR of the quartiles) flags 1 to 3 contacts per mouse and 4 over all mice in these files (11 if each animal's flags are summed), where the paper excludes 7 and keeps 25 in every animal. Which 7 contacts were excluded, and over which span the RMS was taken? The number kept changes the mouse-level U of the gamma-event and MUA claims (8 or 9, and 6 to 8).

How were the 85th percentiles of each mouse computed (MATLAB prctile or another rule)? With 3 against 3 mice the rule decides whether U is 8 or 9 for the gamma events and 6 to 8 for MUA, so fig7e-gamma-events-mice and fig7f-mua-mice-not-significant are blocked until it is known.

How were gamma events detected in detail (the sampling rate, the jackknife of the 99% confidence interval of the baseline mean amplitude, and whether the 1200 s window starts at the bioluminescence onset or the infusion)? Every reading tried gives about 29 to 34 events per contact in Opsin (+) mice, against the paper's 213.6, and 10 to 13 in Opsin (-) against 139.3.

Which baseline values does the test for a contact exceeding baseline bootstrap? With the 180 one-second spectrogram steps before onset, nearly every contact in both groups exceeds baseline (22 to 31 per mouse), against the paper's 15.7 and 2.7. The same rule on the paper's own Fig. 7d group-mean series counts 20 of 25 Opsin (-) contacts above baseline.

In Supplementary Data 6, the Fig. 6f column "Synaptic blockers (After)" has 18 values, identical to the first "Synaptic blockers (After)" column of Fig. 4e in Supplementary Data 4, where the Fig. 6f legend gives n = 21. On these columns the Mann-Whitney test gives p = 3.6e-10, against the legend's p = 0.7870. The 21-value column of the same name in Fig. 5c gives p = 0.534, so the data behind the legend's test are not among the published columns.

entries.name: prakash-2022
entries.title: Interluminescence in culture and in vivo (Prakash et al. 2022)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Prakash et al. (2022) on dandiset 000935, which holds the in vivo experiment of Figure 7, laminar recordings and bioluminescence imaging in six PV-Cre mice given CTZ over barrel cortex, three with a postsynaptic opsin and three without. The in vitro findings of Figures 2 to 6 are tested on the per-electrode spike counts the article publishes as Supplementary Data 1 to 6, as the dandiset does not hold the culture recordings.
